source_title: Uttar Pradesh MLC results: Samajwadi Party makes gains in ahead of assembly polls - India Today
source_excerpt:
UP MLC election results: The Samajwadi Party won five of 11 seats on offer in Uttar Pradesh, a gain of two.
Akhilesh Yadav's Samajwadi Party received a boost in Uttar Pradesh ahead of next year's assembly polls, winning five out of 11 MLC seats that were on offer in the latest round of polls. The BJP won the remaining 6. While the BJP retained its pre-poll tally, the SP marked a gain of two seats, which will work as a psychological booster for the party in the poll-bound state.
Among the seats won by the SP were two seats in Varanasi. The Samajwadi Party retained both the Varanasi Teachers' MLC seat and the Varanasi Graduates' constituency. Varanasi is the Parliamentary constituency of Prime Minister Narendra Modi .
The SP also won the Lucknow Graduates', Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates', and the Agra Teachers' constituencies . The BJP secured victories in the Lucknow Teachers', Meerut-Saharanpur Teachers', Meerut-Saharanpur Graduates', Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers', and Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers' constituencies.
The results are significant as UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath campaigned for the BJP candidates on every seat. The Samajwadi Party, on the other hand, relied largely on its local leaders to garner support.
Now, you must be wondering what are graduates' and teachers' constituencies? These constituencies exist in states that have a legislature with two houses - the assembly and the council.
At the time of the drafting of the Constitution, there was a feeling that having some members of the Council elected only by the educated would help reduce the effects of caste, religion, money or muscle power.
Thus, MLC elections for graduates' and teachers' constituencies use preferential voting. Only registered graduates or teachers are eligible to vote, not the general public.
Coming back to the UP MLC election results. VARANASI MLC ELECTION RESULTS 2026
The two constituencies in Varanasi were the most closely watched, given that they fall within the Prime Minister's constituency.
While MLC elections are not a direct reflection of voter mood, they do offer clues to regional power equations, party organisation and the local-level challenges.
In the Varanasi Teachers' seat, SP's Lal Bihari Yadav defeated BJP's Pramod Kumar Mishra by 4,898 votes. In 2020, Mishra, then contesting as an Independent, lost to him by only 936 votes.
On the other hand, Samajwadi Party's Ashutosh Sinha decisively won the Varanasi Graduates' constituency against BJP candidate Kedar Nath Singh.
Yadav said teachers stood firmly with the Samajwadi Party and credited party chief Akhilesh Yadav for his victory. "The party has been able to contest strongly across all seats in UP because of the positive approach of our national president," Yadav told ANI.
He said that just as 'Netaji' was regarded as a leader of teachers, Akhilesh shared the same outlook. Samajwadi Party stalwart and Akhilesh's father Mulayam Singh Yadav was fondly called 'Netaji' by his supporters.
Yadav asserted that the contentious UGC Bill, which proposed regulations to address caste-based discrimination in universities, had no impact on the election. The legislation has been stayed by the Supreme Court.
"The UGC bill had no impact on our election, because the people associated with the UGC bill remained divided among themselves. The people who wanted job security stayed with us," he further said. WHAT DOES SP'S WIN IN VARANASI MEAN?
Samajwadi Party leaders described the victory as a bellwether for next year's Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, stressing that it signals shifting sentiment in the BJP's stronghold.
Several SP leaders pointed to PM Modi's lower victory margin in the 2024 Varanasi Lok Sabha polls compared to the elections in 2019 and 2014. In the 2024 polls, PM Modi was initially trailing before making a stunning comeback to defeat Congress's Ajay Rai by over 1.50 lakh votes.
The Varanasi division covers Varanasi, Chandauli, Ghazipur, Jaunpur, Mirzapur, Sonbhadra, Bhadohi and Ballia districts.
For Akhilesh Yadav, the strong showing in Varanasi offers a significant psychological boost and bragging rights ahead of the big battle in 2027.
"Teachers have received nothing but humiliation from the BJP. Every teacher will remember the conspiracy to make them perform the most degrading and unwanted task of collecting fodder. They will fulfil their 'Guru Sankalp' by defeating the BJP in the 2027 elections," Akhilesh tweeted.
For the BJP, it is a setback in PM Modi's constituency. It signals localised discontent and policy-related concerns among middle-class voters.
The BJP, which suffered a jolt in the 2024 Lok Sabha election when its Uttar Pradesh tally fell to 33 from 62 in 2019, was looking to increase its tally in the Legislative Council to send a message that it had regained ground.
"A few months to UP polls, the BJP losing in PM's own constituency and that too to educated votes from teachers and graduate communities is big," tweeted Congress leader Srivatsa.
However, despite the high-stakes loss in Varanasi, the BJP delivered a strong overall performance across other regions of the state, successfully guarding its turf in western and northern Uttar Pradesh. - Ends
